routes.label: Split at the two known abscissas and solve affine equations

question: The graphs of \(y = -|x - a| + b\) and \(y = |x - c| + d\) intersect at points \((2, 5)\) and \((8, 3).\) Find \(a + c.\)
solution:
Both given points lie on each graph. Subtracting their equations removes the vertical shifts \(b\) and \(d\), leaving conditions on \(a\) and \(c\).

For the downward-opening graph,
\[
5=-|2-a|+b,\qquad 3=-|8-a|+b,
\]
so \(|8-a|-|2-a|=2\). For the upward-opening graph, subtraction similarly gives \(|8-c|-|2-c|=-2\).

To solve both equations at once, define
\[
D(t)=|8-t|-|2-t|.
\]
The signs inside the absolute values change only at 2 and 8, so the complete case split is
\[
D(t)=
\begin{cases}
6,&t<2,\\
10-2t,&2\le t\le8,\\
-6,&t>8.
\end{cases}
\]
For example, in the middle interval the difference is \((8-t)-(t-2)=10-2t\). The outer cases cannot give either 2 or \(-2\). Thus
\[
10-2a=2,\qquad 10-2c=-2,
\]
which give \(a=4\) and \(c=6\). Substitution gives \(b=7\) and \(d=1\); these values make both graphs pass through both specified points.

Therefore \(a+c=4+6=\boxed{10}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
